title: add CUDA graph capture/replay support with shape guards and warmup to reduce kernel launch overhead
author: Evelyn Park
description: Motivation: reduce per-token kernel launch overhead on long-running sessions by capturing common execution graphs and replaying them with minimal scheduling cost. This PR implements CUDA graph capture/replay for the inference runtime, adds shape guards to ensure captured graphs are valid across nearby sequence-length/beam-size variants, and introduces an adaptive warmup path that falls back to legacy execution while the graph is being populated. Changes are opt-in behind runtime config; default rollout for dedicated pools. Checklist: [x] implement graph capture/replay API, [x] add shape-guarding logic with hashed signature, [x] add warmup mode and telemetry, [x] integrate with continuous batching and KV cache, [x] add unit + integration tests, [x] performance benchmarks and stability runs. Testing notes: microbenchmarks show 18-35% p99 token latency reduction in common chat workloads after warm caches; initially observed an intermittent regression in KV-cache lookup latency due to ordering assumptions which is fixed in commit 6. Rollout plan: feature flag gated, enable for rollout group 10% then ramp to 100% after 1 week of SLO telemetry. Related: ENG-5123 (perf initiative), ENG-4988 (regression debugging).
commits: feat(runtime): add cuda graph capture and replay primitives
perf(runtime): add shape guard checking and signature hashing
fix(runtime): avoid KV-cache ordering regression when replay is used
test(runtime): add integration tests for capture/replay warmup path
ci: add perf benchmark job for cuda graph runs
changed_snippets:
// warmup: replay a small number of steps to populate KV cache before fast path
for (int i=0; i < warmup_steps; ++i) replay_step(ctx);
review_comments: Kai Lin (2026-02-11): Nice work. Can you clarify how signature hashing handles attention-mask differences? We need deterministic guarding for prefix caching.
Evelyn Park (2026-02-11): The signature includes normalized mask shape and a mask-type enum; comment added and tests extended to cover prefix vs full attention masks.
Miguel Santos (2026-02-13): I saw a flaky CI failure in perf/regression suite; TRACE shows different enqueue ordering under capture. Is the KV-cache insertion order stable?

Evelyn Park (2026-02-14): Good catch — ordering assumption fixed in commit 'fix(runtime): avoid KV-cache ordering regression when replay is used' and added a test to assert deterministic insertion order.
Jordan Patel (2026-02-17): Approving on perf numbers, but please add a runtime flag to disable graph replay per-model for quick rollback.
Evelyn Park (2026-02-18): Added per-model override flag and runtime_flags.yaml entry; updated docs and rollout plan.
Kai Lin (2026-02-19): CI perf job passed and benchmarks look solid. Approving merge.
Miguel Santos (2026-02-19): Verified on dedicated infra; 25% p99 improvement on low-latency config. Approved.
release_notes: Added experimental CUDA graph capture/replay to runtime with shape guards and adaptive warmup. Expect reduced p99/token latency for warmed workloads. Feature is gated by runtime flag and rollout is gradual. Includes fixes for KV-cache ordering regression observed during early runs.
regression_note: During internal perf runs a regression was observed where KV-cache insertion order changed under replay, causing correctness failures for some attention-prefix workloads; the issue was fixed by ensuring deterministic KV insertion ordering and adding tests to prevent recurrence.
